readiness.title: Find your next practical step.
readiness.intro: Review eleven parts of your AML/CTF arrangements. Mark what is in place, what needs work and what you need to clarify.
readiness.scope_note: First, confirm which services bring your business into scope. Use the sector guides or discuss your services with us. This check does not determine whether the Act applies.

questions.title: Enrolment
questions.question: Is your business enrolled and its AUSTRAC information current?

questions.title: Risk assessment
questions.question: Have you documented and reviewed the risks your business faces?

questions.title: Written program
questions.question: Do staff follow documented policies and procedures?

questions.title: Approval and oversight
questions.question: Is the program approved by a senior manager and overseen by your governing body?

questions.title: Compliance officer
questions.question: Is an appropriate management-level officer appointed and carrying out the role?

questions.title: Initial CDD
questions.question: Do you establish customer identity, ownership, purpose and risk before service, subject to permitted exceptions?

questions.title: Ongoing CDD
questions.question: Do you review changes, update information and address unusual activity?

questions.title: Existing customer reviews
questions.question: Have you recorded your existing customers’ risk ratings, where required, and set risk-based periodic CDD review dates?
questions.note: Use your program’s categories, such as low, medium or high. Apply the special rules for pre-commencement customers and review sooner when circumstances change.

questions.title: Reporting
questions.question: Can your team identify, assess and submit required reports within applicable deadlines?

questions.title: Records and people
questions.question: Are records retained and relevant personnel checked and trained?

questions.title: Independent evaluation
questions.question: Have you arranged evaluation within the applicable timetable?

readiness.result_note: These are your own responses, not an assessment or certification of compliance. A complete review must consider your services and circumstances.
readiness.privacy_note_if_true: Answers stay in this page during your visit. They are not saved or sent to Nimbi.

result_rules.unanswered: Show remaining questions, not a result.
result_rules.needs_work: List those topics under Needs attention.
result_rules.not_sure: List those topics under Clarify next.
result_rules.all_in_place: You have marked these areas as in place. Keep the supporting evidence current and continue required reviews.
result_rules.never: No score, percentage, green compliant badge, pass/fail or automatic legal determination.

applicability.title: First, check the services you provide.
applicability.intro: Choose your sector and answer for work carried out in the course of business. These questions identify matters to check against the Act and Rules; they are not a legal determination. A geographical link to Australia and any relevant exclusions or exemptions must also be considered.

accountants.question: Do you help a client plan or carry out a sale, purchase or transfer of real estate?
accountants.note: Consider work that directly advances a transaction, rather than general advice alone. Services pursuant to or resulting from a court or tribunal order have an exclusion; earlier work needs its own assessment.

accountants.question: Do you help a client buy, sell or transfer a controlling interest in a legal entity or arrangement?
accountants.note: Assess the transaction and the role you perform. A hypothetical sale or general tax advice alone is different from acting to progress a transaction.

accountants.question: Do you receive, hold, control or manage client money or property to assist a transaction?
accountants.note: Relevant exceptions include payment for your own services and specified court or government payments. Incidental handling for non-designated work is conditional and depends on the business providing no other designated services beyond this client-property service. Select Not sure if an exception may apply.

accountants.question: Do you help organise or carry out equity or debt financing for a legal entity or arrangement?
accountants.note: Include proposed entities. The work must directly advance the financing, rather than only provide general information about options.

accountants.question: Do you help create or restructure legal entities or arrangements, including SMSF trusts?
accountants.note: The scope includes relevant preparatory steps. Testamentary trusts are excluded. Whether detailed advice itself advances a structure depends on what it enables the client to do.

accountants.question: Do you act as, or arrange someone to act as, an officeholder, trustee, partner or nominee shareholder for a client?
accountants.note: Other specified positions, including attorneys of entities, may also be relevant. Court-ordered roles and an attorney for an individual require separate consideration under the precise service definition.

accountants.question: Do you provide a registered office or principal business address for a client entity, or sell or transfer a shelf company?
accountants.note: These are separate designated-service categories. Check the exact activities performed and any applicable exemptions.

real_estate.question: Do you broker property sales or transfers for sellers, for commission or other consideration?
real_estate.note: Both buyer and seller are customers of the brokerage service. The definition covers specified interests in Australian land, including leases longer than 30 years; it excludes some other interests.

real_estate.question: Do you act as a buyers’ agent to find, negotiate or buy real estate for a fee or commission?
real_estate.note: The buyer relationship starts when the agreement to find or identify a property is signed. The seller is also a customer when the transaction is reasonably expected to proceed.

real_estate.question: Does your business sell or transfer real estate directly to buyers, without an independent agent brokering the sale, as a business of selling real estate?
real_estate.note: Include off-the-plan property, subdivisions and sales through in-house staff. Construction alone and a one-off sale of your own premises are different. Assess the selling entity; select Not sure if a related entity or agency arrangement makes the position unclear.

result_rules.any_yes: Your responses identify services that may bring your business into scope. Confirm the exact service definitions, geographical link and any exclusions or exemptions before deciding your obligations.
result_rules.any_unsure_no_yes: Some services need clarifying. A scope discussion can help establish which obligations apply.
result_rules.all_no: Your answers have not identified one of the services covered by this short check. This does not confirm that your business is outside the Act; other services or circumstances may be relevant.
result_rules.incomplete: Complete the remaining questions to see the areas to check.
result_rules.priority: If Yes and Not sure both occur, show possible designated services plus a separate list of uncertainties.
